issues.description: resolve(from, '..', s || '') — the precondition on `from` is unstated and the change is unproven
issues.detail: The diff silently changes the meaning of `resolveSources`. Previously `resolve(s, from)` was called; now it is `resolve(from, '..', s || '')`. The author appears to have assumed that `from` is always a file path, so that `../s` resolves relative to the directory of `from`. State the precondition: is `from` guaranteed to be a file (not a directory, not a URL, not a bare specifier)? If `from` is a directory, `..` walks one level too high; if `from` is a URL, `pathe.resolve` behavior is silently wrong. No invariant, no test pinning this behavior at this layer. The change may be correct for the observed cases, but it has not been reasoned about — it has been tested against a snapshot.

issues.description: getSourceMap callback silently swallows the absent-map case by falling off the end
issues.detail: The new `getSourceMap(file)` returns `extractSourcemapFromFile(...)` when the module has no transform result and the file exists, and otherwise returns `undefined` implicitly. There are three distinct cases — (a) inlined module, do nothing; (b) external module, file missing; (c) external module, file present but no map. All three collapse into `undefined`. State the postcondition: caller receives `SourceMap | undefined`, and `undefined` means 'apply no remapping'. Fine — but the comment claims this 'only handles external modules', which is a property of the call site, not a property enforced here. A reader cannot follow the control flow without simulating it. Make the cases explicit, or document the disjunction precisely.

issues.description: Synchronous readFileSync on every external-frame stack parse — termination/cost not reasoned about
issues.detail: `getSourceMap` is invoked per frame during error stack parsing. Each call may `existsSync` + `readFileSync` the file, then `convert-source-map` may invoke the readMap callback which again `existsSync` + `readFileSync`s a referenced map file. There is no memoization, no cache, no bound on how often the same external file is read for a single error. For an error with N frames touching the same external module, the work is O(N) disk reads of the same bytes. State the termination/cost function. If errors with deep stacks are rare this is acceptable; if they are not, this is a performance bug waiting to be tested-not-proved.

issues.description: extractSourcemapFromFile uses the '{}' string as a fallback map — a smuggled defensive guard
issues.detail: `createConvertSourceMapReadMap` returns the literal string `'{}'` when the referenced map file does not exist. This is defensive-as-substitute: the function pretends to return a valid source map JSON when it cannot. `convert-source-map` will parse this as an empty object with no `mappings`, no `sources`, no `version` — which is not a valid source map. Whether `convert-source-map` then throws, returns a degenerate object, or silently misbehaves depends on its internals. The precondition the caller expects ('returns source content as string, possibly empty') is conflated with 'returns a JSON-shaped placeholder'. A cleaner discipline: return `''` and let the upstream `fromMapFileSource` produce `null`, which the `||` chain already handles.

issues.description: Snapshot is the only correctness witness — TESTED-NOT-PROVED
issues.detail: The behavioral change is asserted by a single updated snapshot that now points at `.ts` line numbers instead of `.js` line numbers. Snapshot equality demonstrates the new output equals the new expected output; it does not demonstrate that the source-map application is correct. No unit test pins `extractSourcemapFromFile` against a known map, no test pins the `resolve(from, '..', s)` change against a fixture with non-trivial `sources` entries (absolute, relative, URL, missing). Testing shows the presence of bugs, not their absence — and here it does not even show that.

issues.description: Module-graph lookup `getModuleById(file)` assumes `file` is a normalized module id
issues.detail: `parseErrorStacktrace` hands the source-map callback whatever string appears in the frame's file position. `project.vite.moduleGraph.getModuleById(file)` expects a Vite module id, which is not necessarily the same string as a stack-trace file path (querystrings, leading slashes on Windows, virtual ids, file URLs). When the lookup misses for reasons unrelated to whether the module is external, the code falls through to `existsSync(file)` and may read and apply a source map for an inlined module whose transform result was simply not found by id. The precondition 'getModuleById returns the module iff it is inlined' is not established.

review.summary: The patch corrects a real bug — external module stack traces were not being source-mapped — and the direction is right. But the work is TESTED-NOT-PROVED. The `resolve(from, '..', s || '')` change has an unstated precondition on `from`; the new `getSourceMap` callback conflates three distinct cases under a single implicit `undefined` return; the readMap fallback returns the string `'{}'` as a defensive placeholder where `''` would be more honest; and the only correctness witness is an updated snapshot. None of this is fatal, but none of it has been reasoned about — the author should state the precondition on `from`, write a unit test that pins `extractSourcemapFromFile` against fixed inputs, and either memoize or document the per-frame I/O cost. Verdict: REASONED-INSUFFICIENTLY. Acceptable to land if a maintainer signs off on the spec the author has not written down; refused on Dijkstra's discipline.
